title: Poland's ePUAP e-government platform restricted after cyberattack; full operation restored 19 November, COI says
date_note: Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski announced the attack on 10 November (per PAP via money.pl); the COI statement of full restoration on 19 November was published by Sekurak on 21 November.
geo_basis: national agency headquarters (Ministry of Digital Affairs / COI), city not stated in the sources
summary: Poland's Centralny Ośrodek Informatyki told Sekurak that access to ePUAP was preventively restricted from 10 November, that the attack was detected and stopped, and that full operation returned on 19 November. Deputy PM Krzysztof Gawkowski said the attack came from abroad and that logs showed preparation for an operation against public administration planned for December. The ABW is investigating; COI says it found no sign of spread beyond the identified area.
plain: Poland's national online platform for government services was restricted for several days after a cyberattack. The government says the attack was stopped and the platform is fully working again.
exec: A national citizen-services portal was restricted for about nine days; officials say a wider attack on administration was planned for December.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Organisations in Polish public administration should follow official communications from the Ministry of Digital Affairs and COI.
impact: Access to ePUAP preventively restricted from 10 to 19 November, with services restored in stages.

validation.note: Sekurak (quoting COI's written answers) and money.pl/PAP (quoting Gawkowski) each state that an attack on ePUAP was stopped. No page from the ministry or COI itself was read.
